classification.difficultyReason: Relate the rectangle width to a semicircular arc, model surface area, verify a maximum using the second derivative and interpret the radius as height.

content.prompt:
A half-pipe is to be made from a rectangular piece of metal of length $x$ m.
The perimeter of the rectangle is $30$ m.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 19, diagram below the prompt on the left
spec.description: Open semicylindrical sheet in perspective, with two curved end profiles joined by two longitudinal rims. The length x labels the lower-right rim. No end plates, radius labels or numerical dimensions are added. The exposed rear-right curved rim joins the outer longitudinal silhouette; the occluded central rear arc remains omitted. The silhouette follows the tangent of the end profile parallel to the extrusion, preserving the open sheet rather than adding end plates.
spec.mathematics: The rectangle length is x; its other dimension becomes the semicircular arc length πr. The half-pipe height is r.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied x label is visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the dimensions of the rectangle that will give the maximum surface area.

answer.worked:
Let the semicircular cross-section have radius $r$ metres. The width of the rectangle is $\pi r$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}30&=2x+2\pi r\\15&=x+\pi r\\x&=15-\pi r\end{align*}$$
The restrictions are $r>0$ and $x>0$, so $0<r<\frac{15}{\pi}$.
The surface area is
$$\begin{align*}S&=\pi rx\\S&=\pi r(15-\pi r)\\S&=15\pi r-\pi^2r^2\\S'&=15\pi-2\pi^2r\end{align*}$$
At a stationary point,
$$\begin{align*}0&=15\pi-2\pi^2r\\r&=\frac{15}{2\pi}.\end{align*}$$
Since $S''=-2\pi^2<0$ throughout the domain, this gives the maximum surface area.
$$\begin{align*}x&=15-\pi\left(\frac{15}{2\pi}\right)\\x&=7.5\text{ m}\\\pi r&=\pi\left(\frac{15}{2\pi}\right)\\\pi r&=7.5\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The rectangle must be $7.5$ m by $7.5$ m.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the height from the ground up to the top of the half-pipe with this maximum area, correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
The cross-section is a semicircle, so the height is its radius.
$$\begin{align*}h&=r\\h&=\frac{15}{2\pi}\text{ m}\\h&\approx2.4\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 decimal place).}\end{align*}$$
